factors.label: Rope tension imbalance
factors.meaning: how unevenly the ropes share the car's weight - the most-loaded rope wears fastest

factors.label: Imbalance growth rate
factors.meaning: how quickly that unevenness is growing day by day

factors.label: Vibration RMS
factors.meaning: how much the ropes and car shake overall

factors.label: Rope-sway band energy
factors.meaning: sway energy - the car swinging side to side because the ropes are not equally tight

factors.label: Mean tension deviation
factors.meaning: tension drift - how far the average rope tension has moved from its commissioning value

factors.label: Fatigue life consumed
factors.meaning: how much of the ropes' rated bending life has already been used (Feyrer)

layman: Rope R6 is carrying 19% more load than the average rope in this set (safe limit: 10%). Think of 6 people carrying one stretcher. If one person carries more, that person tires first. Because rope fatigue rises steeply with load (Feyrer, exponent 4.5), this rope is wearing about 2.2x faster than the others. On the current trend the rope set reaches the end of its safe life in about 10 days. The imbalance is still widening by 0.29 percentage points per day.
causes: possible: uneven rope length after installation or re-roping (one rope shorter, so it takes more load)
possible: worn or undercut groove under rope R6 changing its effective diameter
possible: broken wires or a crushed section in the most-loaded rope
possible: rope stretch (constructional stretch of newer ropes in a mixed set)
possible: car sway from slack ropes or worn guide shoes feeding rope vibration
possible: rope set near the end of its bending-fatigue life, so small differences show as wear

recommendation.why: industry practice is to replace ropes as a set when any rope reaches its discard criteria; R6 is over the 10% limit and 62% of the set's rated bending life is used
recommendation.replace_as_set_note: Industry practice: when any rope reaches its discard criteria, replace the whole set so all ropes have the same diameter, stretch and stiffness.
